doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Playing Bix's cornet and Louis Armstrong's horns
summary: He played Bix's Bach cornet and an Armstrong horn from Queens College at the concert, with jokes about DNA.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did I read that you used some of his own instruments on that?

Oh yeah. That was kind of an interesting thing. And well George was kind of responsible for getting, there’s this couple, Bob Christensen and his wife, that live in California. And they have Bix Beiderbecke’s cornet. It was engraved with his name on it and everything like that. A Bach, this silver Bach cornet. And they just agreed to come to the concert at their own expense and lend us the cornet, and I had never met these people. And it was unbelievable. And then of course there’s the Louis Armstrong Archive at Queens College, and a guy named Michael Cogswell is kind of a friend, is the curator there. And part of that, of what they have, is six or seven horns that belonged to Louis. So I went out there. He let me play them, one other time, and he graciously lent us one for the concert, so I went over there and I picked one that I liked. And I’d never played the Bix horn until a half hour before the concert.

Yeah. And I kind of assumed that it was going to be in real bad shape and probably had never been cleaned out, that it was leaky, you know. But the thing just played great. It was like the best cornet that I’d ever played. So we were thinking we would just kind of display them in the front. But we didn’t know that we would actually play the horns. We ended up, and then the second half, Nicholas tried the Selmer trumpet of Louis’ and the first thing he says was, “where can I get one of these?” So he ended up playing that for the second half. It was very moving.
Did they make him wear white gloves when he played? I got to visit out there and every time he would take something off the shelf—
Yeah. Very, very — treated with great respect.

No, he’s great. He’s really doing a fantastic job with that stuff. He didn’t make me wear white gloves. He maybe should have. But I said just before I played them that — to the © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
audience, I said I almost hesitate to do this because there might still be a little DNA in there and we could clone these guys. I don’t want to do anything that might —
Get saliva samples from the horn. That’s wild.
Right. But that was a thrill, it was a real thrill.
